Age of Intelligence

Choose your people. You lead them from the Stone Age to the stars, and their strengths stay with you all game.

Treasure chests are hidden around the map. Send any unit to one to open it.

Age of Intelligence — Phase 8

Grow your village, raise an army and advance through eight ages on the ground (Stone, Bronze, Iron, Medieval, Gunpowder, Industrial, Modern and Near Future), then launch into space for the Orbital Age. A computer opponent lives on the far side of the land (choose Easy, Normal or Hard when you start a new game). Destroy its Town Center, villagers and army to win. In a Practice game there is no opponent: use the practice raids below to test your army.

Mouse

  • Left-click select · drag box-select · Shift+click add/remove
  • Double-click a unit: select all of that type on screen
  • Right-click (or Ctrl+click): move, gather, build, attack an enemy, heal (herbalists), repair (villagers)
  • With a building selected, right-click sets its rally point
  • Two-finger scroll pans · pinch or mouse wheel zooms
  • Minimap: click to jump, right-click to send units
  • REC (top bar) or F9: save this match's recording so the villagers can learn from it

Fighting

  • Every unit has counters. Hover a train button to see Strong vs / Weak vs.
  • Formations (2+ soldiers): Line, Column, Wedge, Loose. Each changes speed, missile damage and charge.
  • Charge: melee troops that run into battle hit extra hard. Spearmen in Line formation brace and stop charges.
  • Speed matters: javelineers and peltasts are fast, brutes, hoplites and mace warriors are slow. Fast troops can catch slow ones; slow ones can't catch fast ones.
  • Running away: melee troops chase a fleeing enemy a bit faster and hit it on the run, every hit makes a runner stumble, and archers aim ahead of moving targets.
  • Morale: troops waver and then rout (white flag) when outnumbered, hit from behind, or when their Standard Bearer dies. They rally after a few seconds.
  • Fast battles (like Rome: Total War): soldiers break into a run for the last few tiles, a charge that lands knocks the enemy back and makes him stumble, and when one unit routs, the panic spreads to its neighbours.
  • Experience: fighting and kills earn up to 9 chevrons: 3 bronze, then 3 silver, then 3 gold. Each one gives more damage and health and steadier nerves.
  • Commander (Town Center, T): one hero on horseback at a time (a Jarl, Lord or Daimyo). Soldiers inside his gold circle hit harder, get extra armour at higher levels, hold their nerve and learn faster. He levels up from 1 to 10 by fighting. With him selected: R Rally (full morale, routing troops turn round) and F Charge! (his troops run in faster and hit with a charge). If he dies, the army is shaken.
  • Treasure chests (glowing, sparkling) are scattered around the map. Walk any unit onto one to open it.
  • The wild: wolves, boars, bears, giant spiders, bandit camps and trolls attack anyone who comes close. The further from towns, the more dangerous. Hunting animals gives food; bandits and trolls guard treasure.
  • Goals (top right) always show what to do next, with a reward for each.
  • Your faction's bonuses are shown when you hover the emblem in the top bar.

God powers (bar on the left)

  • G god hand: hold the mouse on any unit to pick it up, flick and let go to throw it. Let go over your Town Center to sacrifice a villager for prayer power.
  • Y Rain (puts out fires) · U Heal · I Lightning · O Fire · P Harvest. Bronze Age: J Shield · K Meteor · D Tornado. Then left-click where to cast. Each costs prayer power, which refills faster with more villagers, Shrines and Temples.
  • Kind powers (green) build your villagers' Trust. Cruel ones (red) used on your own people build Fear.

Keys

  • Arrow keys / screen edge: move camera · + / − zoom
  • Villager: H house · L lumber camp · N mining camp · M mill · F farm · B barracks · R archery range · T defense post · X spike trap · E shrine
  • Bronze Age villager: Q temple · Z blacksmith · C market · W watch tower
  • Iron Age villager: ⇧S stable · ⇧A siege workshop. Medieval: ⇧K castle · ⇧D wall (press, then drag a line) · ⇧G gate (only your people can walk through; place it on your own wall to swap a piece)
  • Industrial villager: ⇧O refinery (build it by a black oil seep; oil is the fifth resource) · ⇧T factory. Modern: ⇧E airfield. Near Future: ⇧Q power plant (powers your buildings within 9 tiles) · ⇧R robotics lab (needs power)
  • Aircraft fly over walls, water and forests. Only things that shoot (guns, bows, rockets, towers) can hit them.
  • Near Future villager: ⇧L Launch Complex. Select it and press W to launch a colony ship: you reach the Orbital Age and open space.
  • Soldiers: A attack-move · S stop · Z line · X column · C wedge · V loose
  • Town Center: Q villager · W advance to the next age (each age needs certain buildings first: the button tells you which)
  • Barracks: Q W E R T train · Z X C upgrades. Archery Range: Q W E · Z. Stable and Siege Workshop: Q W E. Castle: Q trebuchet. Factory: Q W E. Airfield: Q W E. Robotics Lab: Q W
  • Shift + train = queue 5 · Shift while placing = place several
  • H (nothing selected) jump to Town Center · . next idle villager · Space centre on selection
  • Squads: Ctrl+1–9 (or Option/Alt+1–9) save the selection as a squad · Shift+1–9 add to it · 1–9 select it (twice = jump there). The squad buttons above the minimap do the same with the mouse (＋ Squad saves the selection).
  • F3 pause (you can still look round and give orders) · Delete take down your selected building (an unfinished one gives back what wasn't built yet) or dismiss selected units; press twice for finished ones
  • Esc cancel · ? this help · F10 or ☰ Menu: save, load, surrender, main menu (the game pauses while it is open; it also saves by itself every 5 minutes)
  • F8 all sound on/off · F7 music on/off · both volumes are in ☰ Menu
  • Game speed: the ▶ 1× button in the top bar (click for 2×, 4×, 8×, right-click for normal) or ] faster · [ slower

Space (Orbital Age)

  • ` (the key left of 1) or the Space button in the top bar: switch between the ground and space. Both keep going while you watch the other.
  • Space has its own resources: rare elements (Mining Drones mine asteroids and bring them to a station) and energy (Solar Arrays, more near the sun). Room for ships comes from stations and Habitats.
  • Constructor: E solar array · H habitat · Y shipyard · T defence platform · Q new station (build near your other structures). Station: C constructor · D mining drone. Shipyard: F fighter · V corvette · G frigate.
  • Ships turn before they fly. Fighters fire straight ahead and loop round; corvettes have turrets and shred fighters; frigates turn slowly, have to aim their nose cannon, and break corvettes and stations, but fighters dodge them.
  • Nebulae (purple clouds) hide ships: things inside them see, and are seen, only close up.
  • H select your station · . next idle drone or constructor · R drones bring their load home
  • God powers in space: U heal (repairs your ships and stations) · J shield · I lightning (strikes the nearest enemy ships) · K meteor (leaves a rich asteroid; it hurts your ships too). A selected ship's own key comes first.
  • If you lose everything in space, select your Launch Complex and press W to launch another colony ship.

The Interstellar Age and the aliens

  • Orbital Station: W Interstellar Age (needs a Shipyard) · then E Deflector Shields (+2 armour) · R Plasma Weapons (+25% damage). Shipyard: B Battlecruiser. Constructor: J Jump Gate.
  • The Jump Gate opens a way to the Deep, the aliens' star system, to the right of home. Send ships anywhere over there and they fly through the gate by themselves, or select ships and press Z (or right-click your gate) to jump. If either end of the gate is destroyed, it collapses.
  • The aliens wake a few minutes after the first colony ship reaches orbit. They are living things that heal: Swarmlings, then Spitters, then huge Leviathans. Their Hive Nodes grow creatures and spread, and they raid through the rift below your planet.
  • Destroy the Hive Heart deep in their system to win the game. If the computer opponent does it first, it wins.

Practice

Spawns a red enemy warband at the far side of the map that marches on your town.
